excerpt: const imageResponse = await axios.get(imageUrl, { responseType: 'arraybuffer' });
sink: this MCP server process itself (not Jira) performs axios.get(imageUrl) server-side with zero validation, then uploads the fetched bytes to Jira as an attachment
why: Personally verified addAttachment() (line 365-388): imageUrl has no scheme/host allowlist, no private-IP/metadata-address block, and no redirect restriction before this code's own axios.get fetches it. A caller can point imageUrl at internal/link-local addresses (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints, internal hosts) and the fetched response body is attached to a Jira ticket -- a read-back/exfiltration channel for whatever internal resource was fetched. This is the fetch performed by this code itself, not forwarded to Jira's backend, so it is SSRF plus response exfiltration, not a benign remote-api-wrapper.
